subject: pypa-packaging-handmade

messages.content: You assign semantic types to the inputs and outputs of tools, so that tools can be chained: the output of one tool becomes the input of another. Reply with JSON only.

These tools come from one library:

### is_valid_version
Check whether a string is a valid version under Python's version rules (PEP 440).
wraps packaging.version.Version
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1.0+foo&asd", "1.0rc0", "."
- output, e.g. false, true

### normalize_version
Return the normalized PEP 440 form of a version string, e.g. '1.0-BETA2' -> '1.0b2'.
wraps packaging.version.Version
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "v1.0", "1.0+AbC", "1.0dev"
- output, e.g. "1.0", "1.0+abc", "1.0.dev0"

### version_info
Split a PEP 440 version into its parts: epoch, release numbers, pre-, post- and
wraps packaging.version.Version
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1.0.post1+dev", "1.0a1.post1.dev1", "1.0"
- output, e.g. {"epoch": 0, "release": [1, 0], "pre": null, "post": 1, "dev": null, "local": "dev", "public": "1.0.post1", "base_version": "1.0", "is_prerelease": false, "i..., {"epoch": 0, "release": [1, 0], "pre": ["a", 1], "post": 1, "dev": 1, "local": null, "public": "1.0a1.post1.dev1", "base_version": "1.0", "is_prerelease": tr..., {"epoch": 0, "release": [1, 0], "pre": null, "post": null, "dev": null, "local": null, "public": "1.0", "base_version": "1.0", "is_prerelease": false, "is_po...

### base_version
Return the base version: the epoch and release numbers only, without pre-, post-,
wraps packaging.version.Version.base_version
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1!1.0a1.post5", "1.0a1", "1!1.0a1+deadbeef"
- output, e.g. "1!1.0", "1.0"

### compare_versions
Compare two PEP 440 versions. Returns -1 if version_a is older, 0 if they are equal,
wraps packaging.version.Version
- parameter `version_a` (string), e.g. "1!1.0.dev0", "1!1.0rc0", "1!1.0.dev456+local"
- parameter `version_b` (string), e.g. "1!1.0a0.post0", "1!1.0rc0", "1.0b2.post345.dev456"
- output, e.g. -1, 0, 1

### sort_versions
Sort version strings from oldest to newest (or newest first if descending is true),
wraps packaging.version.Version
- parameter `versions` (array), e.g. ["1.26.20", "2.0.7", "2.2.3"], ["2.25.1", "2.28.2", "2.31.0", "2.32.3"], ["0.4.4", "0.4.5"]
- parameter `descending` (boolean), e.g. true
- output, e.g. ["2.2.3", "2.0.7", "1.26.20"], ["2.32.3", "2.31.0", "2.28.2", "2.25.1"], ["0.4.5", "0.4.4"]

### canonicalize_version
Return the canonical form of a version used for comparing file names: normalized and,
wraps packaging.utils.canonicalize_version
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1.0", "1.0+abc", "1.4.0"
- parameter `strip_trailing_zero` (boolean), e.g. no example
- output, e.g. "1", "1+abc", "1.4"

### is_valid_specifier
Check whether a string is a valid version constraint (specifier set), e.g. '>=1.0,<2'.
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
- parameter `specifier` (string), e.g. ">=1.0,<2", "~=2.2", "==1.*"
- output, e.g. true, false

### version_satisfies
Check whether a version is allowed by a version constraint such as '>=1.0,!=1.3,<2'.
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.contains
- parameter `version` (string), e.g. "1.0.dev0", "0!2", "3.0.dev0"
- parameter `specifier` (string), e.g. ">=0.9,!=0.9,<=1.0", "==2.*", ">=1,!=1.*,!=2.*,!=3.0,!=3.1,<4"
- parameter `include_prereleases` (boolean/null), e.g. false, true
- output, e.g. false, true

### filter_versions
Keep only the versions allowed by a version constraint, in their original order.
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.filter
- parameter `versions` (array), e.g. ["0.9", "1.0", "1.5", "2.0"], ["1.0", "1.5a1"], ["1.0", "2.0a1"]
- parameter `specifier` (string), e.g. "==1.*,>=1.0", ">=1.0,<=2.0dev", ">=1.0"
- parameter `include_prereleases` (boolean/null), e.g. true, false
- output, e.g. ["1.0", "1.5"], ["1.0", "1.5a1"], ["1.0", "2.0a1"]

### combine_specifiers
Combine two version constraints into one that requires both, e.g. '>=1.0' and '<2' ->
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
- parameter `specifier_a` (string), e.g. ">=1.0", "!=1.5", ">=3.9"
- parameter `specifier_b` (string), e.g. "<2", "~=1.4", "<3.13"
- output, e.g. "<2,>=1.0", "!=1.5,~=1.4", "<3.13,>=3.9"

### is_satisfiable
Check whether at least one version could satisfy a version constraint, e.g.
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.is_unsatisfiable
- parameter `specifier` (string), e.g. "==1.0,>=2.0", "==1.0+local1,!=1.0+local2", "~=1.0a1,<1.0"
- output, e.g. false, true

### specifier_is_subset
Check whether every version allowed by `specifier` is also allowed by `other`, e.g.
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.is_subset
- parameter `specifier` (string), e.g. "", ">=3.12,<3.13", ">=2.0,<1.0"
- parameter `other` (string), e.g. ">=3.12", ">=3.11,<3.13", ">=3.12,<3.12.5"
- parameter `include_prereleases` (boolean/null), e.g. false, true
- output, e.g. false, true

### specifiers_overlap
Check whether at least one version is allowed by both version constraints.
wraps packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet.is_disjoint
- parameter `specifier_a` (string), e.g. ">=1.0", "<1.0", "==1.5"
- parameter `specifier_b` (string), e.g. "<2", ">=2", ">=1.0,<2"
- output, e.g. true, false

### parse_requirement
Parse a dependency line such as 'requests[socks]>=2.31; python_version < "3.13"' into
wraps packaging.requirements.Requirement
- parameter `requirement` (string), e.g. "urllib3>=1.26.20", "Requests", "NumPy; platform_machine == \"arm64\""
- output, e.g. {"name": "urllib3", "extras": [], "specifier": ">=1.26.20", "marker": null, "url": null}, {"name": "Requests", "extras": [], "specifier": "", "marker": null, "url": null}, {"name": "NumPy", "extras": [], "specifier": "", "marker": "platform_machine == \"arm64\"", "url": null}

### evaluate_marker
Evaluate an environment marker such as 'python_version < "3.11" and sys_platform ==
wraps packaging.markers.Marker.evaluate
- parameter `marker` (string), e.g. "extra == 'security'", "extra == 'Different.punctuation..is...equal'", "os_name == 'foo'"
- parameter `environment` (null/object), e.g. {"extra": "quux"}, {"extra": "different__punctuation_is_EQUAL"}, {"os_name": "bar"}
- output, e.g. false, true

### canonicalize_name
Return the normalized project name used by package indexes, e.g. 'Typing_Extensions' ->
wraps packaging.utils.canonicalize_name
- parameter `name` (string), e.g. "fOo", "foo----bar", "Foo"
- output, e.g. "foo", "foo-bar"

### parse_wheel_filename
Parse a wheel file name such as 'numpy-2.1.0-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl'
wraps packaging.utils.parse_wheel_filename
- parameter `filename` (string), e.g. "pyvirtualcam-0.13.0-cp310-cp310-manylinux2014_x86_64.manylinux_2_17_x86_64.whl", "foo-2-py2.py3-none-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.manylinux2014_x86_64.whl", "foo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl"
- output, e.g. {"name": "pyvirtualcam", "version": "0.13.0", "build_tag": null, "tags": ["cp310-cp310-manylinux2014_x86_64", "cp310-cp310-manylinux_2_17_x86_64"]}, {"name": "foo", "version": "2", "build_tag": null, "tags": ["py2-none-manylinux2014_x86_64", "py2-none-manylinux_2_17_x86_64", "py3-none-manylinux2014_x86_64..., {"name": "foo", "version": "1.0", "build_tag": null, "tags": ["py3-none-any"]}

### parse_sdist_filename
Parse a source distribution file name such as 'requests-2.31.0.tar.gz' into project name
wraps packaging.utils.parse_sdist_filename
- parameter `filename` (string), e.g. "requests-2.32.3.tar.gz", "numpy-2.1.3.tar.gz", "typing_extensions-4.12.2.tar.gz"
- output, e.g. {"name": "requests", "version": "2.32.3"}, {"name": "numpy", "version": "2.1.3"}, {"name": "typing-extensions", "version": "4.12.2"}

### parse_tag
Expand a compressed compatibility tag such as 'py2.py3-none-any' into the individual
wraps packaging.tags.parse_tag
- parameter `tag` (string), e.g. "py3-none-any", "cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_17_x86_64", "py2.py3-none-any"
- output, e.g. ["py3-none-any"], ["cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_17_x86_64"], ["py2-none-any", "py3-none-any"]

### supported_tags
List the wheel tags a CPython interpreter accepts, most preferred first.
wraps packaging.tags.compatible_tags
- parameter `python_version` (string), e.g. "3.12", "3.11", "3.10"
- parameter `platforms` (array), e.g. ["manylinux_2_17_x86_64"], ["macosx_11_0_arm64"], ["win_amd64", "linux_x86_64"]
- output, e.g. ["cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_17_x86_64", "cp312-abi3-manylinux_2_17_x86_64", "cp312-none-manylinux_2_17_x86_64", "cp311-abi3-manylinux_2_17_x86_64", "cp310-abi3..., ["cp311-cp311-macosx_11_0_arm64", "cp311-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64", "cp311-none-macosx_11_0_arm64", "cp310-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64", "cp39-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm6..., ["cp310-cp310-win_amd64", "cp310-cp310-linux_x86_64", "cp310-abi3-win_amd64", "cp310-abi3-linux_x86_64", "cp310-none-win_amd64", "cp310-none-linux_x86_64", "...

Give types to their parameters and outputs.

Step 1: find the kinds of values this library works with. Look at the example values: strings that follow a format or name a specific kind of thing (for example an email address, a date, an identifier) are a kind of value. Give each kind a CamelCase type name, such as `EmailAddress`.
Step 2: give every parameter and every output a type.
- Use the same type for every parameter and output that holds the same kind of value in the same format, across all tools. Two things have the same type only if a value of one can be used as the other.
- Most string parameters hold one of the kinds from step 1. Use plain `string` only for free text that fits no kind.
- A list of values of one type is written `list[TypeName]`.
- An output that is an object can list which of its fields have a type. Leave out the other fields.
- Flags and counts get a plain JSON type: boolean, integer or number.

Reply with one JSON object, types first:
{"types": [{"name": "TypeName", "description": "what it is, with one example value"}],
 "tools": {"tool_name": {"parameters": {"param": "TypeName"}, "output": "TypeName"},
           "other_tool": {"parameters": {"items": "list[TypeName]", "strict": "boolean"}, "output": {"fields": {"name": "OtherType", "all": "list[TypeName]"}}}}}
Include every tool and every parameter.
You assign semantic types to the fields of tool outputs, so that tools can be chained. Reply with JSON only.

These types are used for the inputs of a library's tools:

- `MarkerString`, e.g. "extra == 'security'", "extra == 'Different.punctuation..is...equal'", "os_name == 'foo'"
- `SdistFilename`, e.g. "requests-2.32.3.tar.gz", "numpy-2.1.3.tar.gz", "typing_extensions-4.12.2.tar.gz"
- `SpecifierString`, e.g. ">=1.0,<2", "~=2.2", "==1.*"
- `TagString`, e.g. "py3-none-any", "cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_17_x86_64", "py2.py3-none-any"
- `VersionString`, e.g. "1.0+foo&asd", "1.0rc0", "."
- `WheelFilename`, e.g. "pyvirtualcam-0.13.0-cp310-cp310-manylinux2014_x86_64.man..., "foo-2-py2.py3-none-manylinux_2_17_x86_64.manylinux2014_x..., "foo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl"

These tools return objects. One example output each:

### version_info
{"epoch": 0, "release": [1, 0], "pre": null, "post": 1, "dev": null, "local": "dev", "public": "1.0.post1", "base_version": "1.0", "is_prerelease": false, "is_postrelease": true, "is_devrelease": false}

### parse_requirement
{"name": "urllib3", "extras": [], "specifier": ">=1.26.20", "marker": null, "url": null}

### parse_wheel_filename
{"name": "pyvirtualcam", "version": "0.13.0", "build_tag": null, "tags": ["cp310-cp310-manylinux2014_x86_64", "cp310-cp310-manylinux_2_17_x86_64"]}

### parse_sdist_filename
{"name": "requests", "version": "2.32.3"}

For each tool, say which top-level fields hold a value of one of the types above: `TypeName` for one value, `list[TypeName]` for a list of them. Leave out fields that fit no type.

Reply with one JSON object: {"tool_name": {"field": "TypeName", "other_field": "list[TypeName]"}}
